questions.prompt: With a quarter of Kelly, a 5% risk per trade and a cap of 100%, what position does a probability of 0.53 give?
options: +100% of equity, because any edge hits the cap
questions.explanation: The edge is 2 × 0.53 - 1 = 0.06. A quarter is 0.015 of equity at risk, and 0.015 / 0.05 = 0.3, a long position of 30%.

questions.prompt: The model says 0.45. What does the sizing rule do?
options: Holds nothing, because the probability of up is below 0.5
Goes short 50% of equity, because the edge 2 × 0.45 - 1 = -0.1 is negative
Goes short 100%, because any probability below 0.5 hits the cap
questions.explanation: A negative edge means down is more likely. A quarter of -0.1 is -0.025, and -0.025 / 0.05 = -0.5, a short of 50%.

questions.prompt: Why should the probabilities that feed the sizing rule come from test folds, not from the training days?
options: Because on its training days a model looks more certain than it is, so every position would be too large
Because training days have no labels
Because test folds always have probabilities closer to 0.5 by design
Because the cap only applies to test folds
questions.explanation: Training chose the model's numbers to fit those days, so its probabilities there sit too far from 0.5. The position grows with that distance, so it would be too large.
